title: fix(core/app-shell): accept and resolve an inline `I18nLabel` on an action's `resultDialog` (objectui#9542)
body:
Fixes #9542

Clause-②: no

`@object-ui/core`'s `ResultDialogSpec` claimed in its own docblock to mirror `Action.resultDialog` in `@objectstack/spec` and did not. Four of its members — `title`, `description`, `acknowledge` and `fields[].label` — were hand-written `string` where the contract declares every one of them `I18nLabel`: a plain string **or** an inline per-locale map, both authorized by that type's own docblock and neither deprecated. So this repo refused what the platform accepts, which is `check:spec-symbols`' rule-2 failure class — an alignment CLAIM with a hand copy behind it.

The three steps: derive the members from the contract, do the resolution at the dialog, then delete the workaround objectui#8648 left behind.

## The runtime severity: MEASURED, not restated

The card filed this reading as unverified and asked for confirmation. **Confirmed — and it is a throw, not a mis-render.** A rendering test with a locale-map `title` on the unfixed tree:

```
Error: Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {en, zh-CN}).
 ❯ throwOnInvalidObjectTypeImpl …/react-dom-client.development.js
 ❯ reconcileChildFibersImpl …
 ❯ renderRootSync …
```

Nothing upstream coerces or guards the value first. React 19.2.8 throws at the first such member reached, so the dialog never mounts — on an action that has **already succeeded**, and this dialog is the only place a one-shot reveal is ever shown. Three rendering legs failed this way before the change; the three plain-string legs in the same file passed unchanged, which is the control that makes this a reading about the map arm and nothing else.

⚠️ The card's 2FA / OAuth `client_secret` / backup-code examples are the contract's own illustrations of what `resultDialog` is for. They are **not** a measured population and are not restated as one here.

## What changed

**Derive, do not hand-copy.** `@object-ui/core` already depends on `@objectstack/spec` and already imports `Action` from `@objectstack/spec/ui`, so the contract type is reachable — checked rather than assumed, and no hand-written fallback was needed. The four label members are now indexed-access derivations off the contract's own result-dialog block through two module-local aliases. ⛔ No new exported symbol: the two interfaces stay the only names this module publishes for the block, so the clause-② `no` stands on its terms.

**Resolve at the dialog.** Through `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `resolveI18nLabel`, imported under this package's established `resolveInlineI18nLabel` alias. ⛔ Not `resolveKeyedI18nLabel` — that takes the KEYED vocabulary and these members are the INLINE form. A plain-string label is unaffected: the resolver returns it unchanged and the existing fallback chain still answers for an absent label or a map with no usable entry (the `||` chain is kept over `??` for exactly that reason).

**The workaround is out.** Both action renderers drop `as ActionDef` OPEN-BRACKET `'resultDialog'` CLOSE-BRACKET, so the whole forward is compiler-checked with nothing between it and `ActionDef` again. (Spelled in words: GitHub's body sanitizer eats tag-shaped fragments, and an index into a type is what this sentence is about.)

## Zone-2 mechanism assumptions, each tested

**The locale source — one source, no fork.** All six in-package `resolveInlineI18nLabel` sites trace to the same value, `useObjectTranslation().language` from `@object-ui/i18n`: `AppSidebar` and `UnifiedSidebar` destructure `language` off that hook and pass it directly; `resolveActionParams` takes it threaded in and says so in its own docblock; the three metadata-admin sites take a `locale` prop fed by `useMetadataLocale`, which reads that same `language` and clamps it to that designer's two bundled catalogue locales. The clamp is about the designer's own copy catalogue, not a second source — so the un-clamped `language` is what a runtime surface like this dialog wants, matching the three runtime sites. The dialog already called that hook for `t`.

**The sibling type carries the same drift, and repairing it is FORCED by ruling 5 — measured.** `ResultDialogFieldSpec.label` is the contract's fourth `I18nLabel` member on this block. It is not a scope judgement: with `label` reverted to `string` and everything else in place, `@object-ui/components`' type-check goes red at BOTH forward sites with `TS2322 … Types of property 'label' are incompatible`, because the narrowing assertion that used to absorb it is gone. Deleting the assertions and leaving the sibling drifted do not compose. The ablation was run on disk and restored (`git diff HEAD` empty afterwards).

## Tests

A case that is red before and green after, plus a converted pin that is red under ablation.

- `packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/ActionResultDialog.test.tsx` — three new legs. **Before:** `Tests 3 failed | 3 passed (6)`, all three failing with the React throw above. **After:** green. One leg varies only the display language and asserts the other locale's text is resolved AWAY, so the legs cannot pass by rendering both.
- `packages/components/src/renderers/action/__tests__/action-undeclared-keys-8648.test.ts` — the objectui#8648 ledger leg is converted, not merely deleted. Its `as any` negative was never the workaround: `castBefore` only matches a cast between `schema` and the key, so a write-side `as any` walks straight past it and this is the only leg that refuses it. **Ablation:** re-injecting the narrowing assertion at both sites turns the converted legs red (`Tests 2 failed | 14 passed`); restored, `git diff HEAD` empty.

Commands and exit codes, each captured before any pipe, on `7321c6e3`:

> ⚠️ **Seat note (`domain:ui` seat 3, added after the fact — the dev writes this body once and does not PATCH it).** The head has since moved to `23592bab`, two commits on: one re-attaching the spec-alignment docblock to the interface it describes (the derived aliases had landed between them, detaching the claim and reddening `check:spec-symbols`), and one appending the supersession note to `.changeset/8648-ui-action-four-undeclared-keys.md`. The dev reports every ratchet family re-run green on that head. Independently measured by this seat on `23592bab` at the time of this edit: **29 success · 3 expected skips · 0 non-success**, with four `Test` shards still running. ⛔ The table below is left exactly as authored — it is the reading on `7321c6e3` and is not restated as a reading on the current head.

So the gate's exit 0 does not prove anything about THIS tree's closure. It is reported as it is rather than greened over. The diff adds no new module edge into the console's eager graph — `@objectstack/spec/ui` is already imported eagerly by `AppSidebar` in this same package — so the expected movement is zero, but that is reasoning, not the measurement.

The build had to run before the type-checks: a package type-check ahead of its dependency closure produces `TS6305` false reds. Both readings were taken in that order and both were green.

## Deviations from the declared file surface — two, both declared

1. **`packages/app-shell/src/views/__tests__/ActionResultDialog.test.tsx`** is not on the declared surface, and the dispatch also requires a case that fails before the change and passes after. The card's own example is a locale-map `title` reaching this dialog, and its existing sibling test file is where that lives. Extended rather than stopped, and named here.
2. **A second commit re-attaches the spec-alignment docblock** to the interface it describes. The derived aliases had landed BETWEEN that docblock and the interface, which detached the claim — `attachedDoc` in `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` reads only the LAST leading comment block — and `pnpm check:spec-symbols` went red asking for the ledger entry to be deleted. Moving the aliases above the docblock restores the attachment. ⛔ No gate script was edited.

## Acceptance notes

- **`check:spec-symbols`' rule-2 ledger has no state for "claim now BACKED by derivation".** Measured: with the claim re-attached and the members derived, deleting `ResultDialogFieldSpec` from `CLAIM_DEBT` makes the gate red — ``a spec-alignment claim has nothing behind it`` — so the entry must stay although the debt it records is paid. `CLAIM_DEBT` means unbacked and `CLAIM_ALLOW` means deliberate divergence; a repaired symbol fits neither, so it can never leave the ledger, and the ledger's own burn-down instruction cannot be followed for this class. Left as a finding; a gate change is a maintainer-floor item and ⛔ not this card's.
- **The card's "one package over from where that gate matches by name" is true of rule 1 only.** Rule 2 already covers `@object-ui/core` and had this very symbol ledgered as `CLAIM_DEBT` the whole time. Extending rule 1 is therefore a smaller idea than the card implies — it was the CLAIM half, not the coverage half, that was missing.
- Not filed, noted only: the dialog's `fields` fallback entry spells `label: undefined` explicitly where omission would read the same; nothing carries it.

## What this PR does not touch

Out of scope: `#9572` is not addressed here, and `#8941` remains open — both are neighbours in the same directories on different files, and neither is touched. objectui#8648 is referenced only as the card that left the workaround behind.
